cities.name: Jagdalpur
cities.overview: The main town of the Bastar region, a base for waterfalls, cave systems and the tribal haats (weekly markets) of southern Chhattisgarh.

cities.name: Kawardha
cities.overview: A small town in Kabirdham district at the foot of the Maikal hills, about 120 km from Raipur.

cities.name: Raipur
cities.overview: Chhattisgarh's capital, the base for the temples of Sirpur and Rajim.

cities.name: Bilaspur
cities.overview: A city in the north of the state, close to the forests of Achanakmar.

cities.name: Dantewada
cities.overview: A small Bastar town known for the shrine of the goddess Danteshwari.

cities.name: Rajnandgaon
cities.overview: A town close to the hill shrine at Dongargarh.

cities.name: Ambikapur
cities.overview: The main town of Surguja in the north, close to the plateau of Mainpat.

cities.name: Dhamtari
cities.overview: A town south of Raipur, close to the Gangrel Dam.

places.name: Chitrakote Falls
places.shortDescription: India's widest waterfall, where the Indravati River drops in a horseshoe curve, often called the Niagara of India.
places.description: At Chitrakote the Indravati River plunges about 29 m over a horseshoe-shaped cliff that can stretch roughly 300 m wide in the monsoon. The falls change character through the year, from a roaring red-brown curtain in August to separate silvery streams in the dry season. Boats take visitors close to the base when the water is calm, and viewpoints on the rim catch the evening light. A small Shiva temple stands near the edge.
places.history: The falls lie in Bastar, a region of Gond, Muria and other Adivasi communities whose festivals, such as the 75-day Bastar Dussehra, are among India's most distinctive.
places.bestTimeNote: July to October for full flow; November to February for boat rides and pleasant weather.

places.name: Kanger Valley National Park
places.shortDescription: Sal forests, limestone caves and the Tirathgarh waterfall in a compact national park near Jagdalpur.
places.description: Kanger Valley (Kanger Ghati) National Park follows the Kanger River through dense sal and teak forest. Its best-known sights are Kotumsar Cave, an underground passage of stalactites and blind fish reached by narrow steps, and the tiered Tirathgarh waterfall. The park is also home to the hill myna, the state bird, which mimics human speech. Guides are required inside the caves and the caves close during the monsoon.
places.history: The area was declared a national park in 1982 and takes its name from the Kanger River that runs through it.
places.bestTimeNote: November to April. The park and caves are usually closed in the monsoon (July to October).

entryFee.note: Park entry, vehicle and cave fees are charged separately; guides are mandatory in the caves.

location.address: Kanger Ghati National Park, Darbha, Bastar district, Chhattisgarh

places.name: Bhoramdeo Temple
places.shortDescription: An 11th-century Shiva temple in the Maikal hills, covered in sculpture and often called the Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh.
places.description: Set beside a lake at the foot of the Maikal hills, the Bhoramdeo Temple is a Nagara-style Shiva temple whose outer walls are carved with deities, dancers and amorous couples in the manner of Khajuraho. A few kilometres away are the smaller Madwa Mahal and the brick Cherki Mahal. The surroundings are peaceful and see few outside visitors. A local festival is held here in March.
places.history: The temple is attributed to the Nagavanshi rulers of the region and is generally dated to the late 11th century CE.

places.name: Sirpur
places.shortDescription: An ancient site on the Mahanadi, with the brick Lakshmana Temple and big Buddhist monasteries.
places.description: A rich old capital 78 km from Raipur, with the finely carved brick Lakshmana Temple and excavated Buddhist viharas.
places.history: The Lakshmana Temple dates from the 7th century.

places.name: Rajim
places.shortDescription: A temple town on the sacred meeting of the Mahanadi, Pairi and Sondur rivers.
places.description: Known as the Prayag of Chhattisgarh, with the Rajiv Lochan Temple. A large fair is held here each February.

places.name: Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A forest sanctuary in Mahasamund district, established in 1976, with leopards and gaur.
places.description: Teak and sal forest within reach of Raipur, with jeep safaris and birdwatching.

places.name: Gangrel Dam
places.shortDescription: A large dam across the Mahanadi in Dhamtari, with a beach and water sports.
places.description: The largest reservoir in the state, with a beach-like shore that's popular for weekend water sports.

places.name: Kotumsar Cave
places.shortDescription: A long limestone cave in Kanger Valley near Jagdalpur, known for stalactites and blind fish.
places.description: A guide leads you through narrow passages, with torches on stalactites and blind fish in the pools. It closes during the monsoon.
places.bestTimeNote: Closed in the monsoon, usually from June to October.

places.name: Danteshwari Temple
places.shortDescription: A 14th-century temple at Dantewada, a Shakti Peetha and the patron goddess of Bastar.
places.description: Stone temple at the meeting of two rivers, closely linked to the Bastar Dussehra festival, one of India's longest.
places.bestTimeNote: Parts of Bastar have long-running security issues, so check local advice before going off the main routes.

places.name: Indravati National Park
places.shortDescription: A remote tiger reserve in Bijapur district, on the Indravati River, and among the last homes of wild water buffalo.
places.description: One of the least visited parks in India because of security issues in the area. It's worth learning about, but go only with up-to-date advice.
places.bestTimeNote: Parts of Bastar have long-running security issues, so check local advice before going off the main routes.

places.name: Achanakmar Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A tiger reserve in the Maikal Hills, shared with Madhya Pradesh, close to Bilaspur.
places.description: A sal forest crossed by a road and a rail line, with jeep safaris. Part of the Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve.

places.name: Bambleshwari Temple
places.shortDescription: A hilltop goddess temple at Dongargarh, reached by about a thousand steps or a ropeway.
places.description: Navaratri brings huge crowds to this temple, which is reached by a ropeway. It's a stop on the Mumbai to Howrah line, so many pilgrims arrive by rail.

places.name: Mainpat
places.shortDescription: A cool plateau in Surguja known as the Shimla of Chhattisgarh, with a Tibetan settlement.
places.description: A Tibetan refugee settlement has brought monasteries to this cool, green plateau, and Dalmia Falls are nearby.

places.name: Guru Ghasidas National Park
places.shortDescription: A large tiger reserve in north Chhattisgarh, spread across remote forest and hills.
places.description: Remote sal forest in the north, linked to Bandhavgarh and Palamau. It was declared a tiger reserve along with Tamor Pingla.
